newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Shekel fixed slightly higher against dollar.
newsitem.headline: Shekel fixed slightly higher against dollar.

text.p: The Israeli shekel representative rate was fixed slightly higher against the dollar on Thursday following the weakening of the American currency in world markets, dealers said.
"The shekel was steady, trading in a narrow range during most of the day and rising slightly after the dollar weakened mildly against the mark and yen," said a dealer at United Mizrahi Bank.
"The weakening of the dollar prevented the basket from falling further. The basket was stuck at around 6.92 percent below the diagonal rate," he said.

The shekel is allowed to fluctuate in a trading band of seven percent above or below a sloping mid-point designed to devalue the Israeli currency at a rate of six percent a year against the basket of key currencies.

Although the basket rate was touching bottom, dealers said the Bank of Israel did not intervene in the market today. The central bank entered the market in three of the last six trading sessions in a bid to keep the basket rate within the band, buying what dealers estimated was about 500 million shekels in foreign currency.

The representative rate for the dollar was fixed at 3.2630 shekels against 3.2680 shekels on Wednesday. The basket, composed of the dollar, mark, pound sterling, French franc and yen, was fixed at 3.6186 shekels against 3.6185 on Wednesday.
On the crosses the shekel traded against the yen at 2.7865 shekels per 100 yen against 2.7835 on Wednesday and against the mark at 2.0510 shekels against 2.0451 on Wednesday.
In late afternoon the dollar was trading at 3.2640 shekels.
